base.name: Личинка
base.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. ONE rough enemy silhouette study for a 2D TOP-DOWN survival horror game. Reference roles: Image 1 suggests segmented fleshy parasitic anatomy; Image 2 suggests long grasping clawed limbs; Image 3 suggests elongated neck/spine/tail proportions; Image 4 supplies Emergency Shift's existing pale flesh, dark contour and bone accent drawing style. Invent original anatomy, do not copy any reference character. CRITICAL: References 1 and 3 are SIDE VIEWS, but your output must be a TRUE CEILING VIEW, 90-degree orthographic looking straight down at the TOP OF THE BACK AND SKULL. Creature is running on a horizontal floor below camera, forward direction to the RIGHT of canvas. Show shoulders, spine, hips and each planted foot as their actual overhead footprints. NO upright front-facing body, NO visible chest/belly, NO side profile, NO isometric view, NO face looking at viewer. All limbs extend along the floor plane. The front of the face points horizontally RIGHT, so only the TOP of its head is seen. Make silhouette anatomical and grotesque rather than a geometric badge or a spider with an eye in the middle. Use simple broad desaturated GRAY-PINK FLESH shapes, dark muted rose joint gaps and a few ivory claw tips; 2-3 flat tones, restrained dark outline, only a FEW big segmented/ribbed folds where anatomy requires them. No microtexture, veins, glossy polish, tiny details. No central eye symbol. Complete connected limbs and body; modest asymmetric running pose. Actual transparent background, no text, watermark, floor, glow, cast shadow, grid or frame. ANATOMY: Thick curved segmented worm-like torso with a broad blunt tubular head at the front, NO arms, exactly TWO short strong running legs attached at rear hips. Body is about three times wider than either leg. The dorsal head is a plain rounded fleshy cap, NOT a visible circular mouth looking at the camera. About five large soft segment folds, blunt rear without tail.

edits.prompt: Edit Image 1 only. Image 1 is the chosen Emergency Shift creature and the exact edit target. Image 2 is ONLY a reference for the circular tooth-ring mouth idea, not for color or camera. Keep the chosen creature's entire segmented gray-pink body, two clawed rear legs, all limb joints, overhead pose, silhouette behind the head, paint style and proportions unchanged. At the RIGHTMOST rounded end of its long segmented body, add an integrated short fleshy head with a ROUND OPEN MAW. The open mouth must have a COMPLETE CLOSED 360-DEGREE CIRCUMFERENCE of individual ivory triangular teeth: teeth all the way around TOP, BOTTOM, LEFT and RIGHT, forming one unmistakable full ring pointing inward toward a very dark burgundy throat. Do not leave a toothless half or merely two rows on upper/lower jaws. A restrained second inner row is optional only if it does not obscure the complete outer tooth ring. Gray-pink fleshy circular lip, the same muted flesh palette as the body, not red skin. The head is attached seamlessly to the right end, comparable in width to the front body segment, no long added neck. GAME CAMERA IS DIRECTLY ABOVE, looking down onto the creature's back. The creature's new mouth is tilted UP toward the ceiling camera so the COMPLETE round tooth ring is visible from above; the rest of the creature stays in its exact existing overhead projection, not a side or upright front-view pose. No eyes, face, ears, horns, extra legs, tongue, dripping blood, floor or shadow. Preserve genuine alpha transparency; no checkerboard baked into the pixels. Maintain the original spacious framing and do not crop any foot or head.

Edit Image 1 to apply the placement correction drawn in Image 2. Image 1 is the clean creature edit target. Image 2 is the user's annotated placement guide: the red circle marks the head to MOVE; the red arrow's LEFT tip marks its NEW LOCATION near the base of the torso BETWEEN THE TWO RUNNING LEGS. The arrow means relocation, not a new graphic. Move the COMPLETE circular fleshy head with its 360-degree tooth ring away from the far RIGHT end and integrate it into the UPPER/DORSAL FRONT OF THE CENTRAL BODY at the root between the two legs, approximately halfway across the creature's length. The circular dark maw and the full uninterrupted ring of ivory triangular teeth must remain clearly visible from the overhead camera at this new location. Orient the creature's front toward the left / leg-root region as indicated; the long segmented body section extending to the RIGHT now reads as a tapering rear body/tail, with a simple rounded terminal segment and NO mouth or second head there. Keep the two existing clawed legs, their pose and attachment, fleshy segmented anatomy, pale gray-pink palette, dark outline, overall scale and overhead projection. Show one head only. Do not merely shift the entire creature or leave the mouth on the right tip. No red arrow, red circle, labels or annotations in the result. Actual transparent background with no checkerboard baked into it. No new eyes, extra limbs, gore, floor or cast shadow. This remains a strict 90-degree ceiling view of the body; only the dorsal circular maw is exposed to the ceiling camera. Preserve all existing complete limb tips and roomy framing.

Edit this chosen Emergency Shift monster concept. The camera remains a STRICT ORTHOGRAPHIC CEILING VIEW onto the back, the creature's FRONT is LEFT between the two clawed running legs, its REAR extends RIGHT. Make these two changes while preserving the two existing clawed legs, pose, pale gray-pink fleshy palette, dark outlines and overall organic drawing style. CHANGE 1 — MAW: enlarge the circular fleshy mouth-head at the LEFT between the legs by about 45-55 percent in visible diameter, making it the clear dominant front feature. Tilt the actual fleshy head and mouth FORWARD toward the LEFT / direction of travel by a moderate angle, instead of having the opening point straight vertically at the ceiling. In this true top view, the tilted mouth opening should be a clear foreshortened OVAL (moderately narrower along left-right travel axis), with convincing near/far lip thickness and a short connective neck-root; it must still show the COMPLETE 360-degree continuous ring of ivory triangular teeth around every part of the opening, pointing inward at the dark burgundy throat. Keep the opening visibly angled forward, not just a larger flat circular sticker on its back. No eyeballs, tongue, dripping blood or human facial traits. CHANGE 2 — REAR BODY: the current RIGHT rear torso/tail looks phallic because of its cylindrical sausage shape, repetitive complete rings and smooth rounded terminal cap. REDESIGN that rear anatomy into a LOW FLAT TAPERED WEDGE of living flesh: wider and flattened at the base, angular irregular outer contour, a few staggered broad muscle folds that do NOT wrap around as identical circular rings, and a tapering asymmetrical shallow forked tip instead of any bulbous or rounded cap. The dorsal silhouette should read as a broad muscular back narrowing into a flattened tissue tail, never a penis, tube, glans, mushroom cap or circumferential cuff. Keep it fleshy rather than insect armor; no hard shell, wings, added limbs or scorpion stinger. One larger forward-tilted mouth at the LEFT only. No mouth at the rear. Original actual transparency, no checkerboard baked in, no floor, glow, cast shadow, arrows, labels or text. Complete creature with all feet inside the canvas.

Carefully revise this exact early overhead creature. This is a SMALL CORRECTION, not a new ornate monster. Keep its two existing bent clawed legs, their exact pose and attachments, muted pale gray-pink palette, thin dark contour, simple broad flesh shapes, and strict 90-degree TOP-DOWN camera. Front is LEFT between the two legs; rear is RIGHT. HEAD: enlarge the existing mouth by ONLY about 25 percent compared with this input. Keep it compact and integrated directly into the front body mass. Gently incline the mouth toward the LEFT direction of travel, about 15-20 degrees away from pointing straight up. From the ceiling its opening reads as a modestly foreshortened ellipse, about 0.85 width-to-height, and all of the FULL CIRCUMFERENCE of ivory triangular teeth remains visible as one complete continuous ring. One clear row of roughly 20-24 simple teeth and a dark burgundy interior; few large inner shapes, no tiny flesh frills. The lower/back lip merges immediately into the torso with ONE soft anatomical transition. NO protruding cylindrical neck, no stacked lip rings, no deep barrel, no swollen cuff, no giant trumpet mouth. Do not make the mouth the size of the whole torso. REAR ANATOMY: replace the long cylindrical ringed right portion with a COMPACT FLATTENED ABDOMEN, about 20-25 percent shorter than the old right portion. Broad low oval-to-wedge footprint seen from above, gently asymmetrical, slightly wider near its base, narrowing to a short blunt DIAGONAL end-fold. Use 3-4 large OFFSET flesh lobes with interrupted seams and a subtle lengthwise dorsal groove, rather than complete concentric rings. No separate bulbous terminal segment. No glans-like cap, penis shape, circumferential collar, forked tail, two-pointed tail, fins, ribbons, spikes, flowing cloth folds or hard insect shell. The rear outline should be one simple cohesive low flesh mass. Maintain leg-to-body proportion and overall readable anatomical structure. No new eyes, extra limbs, blood, face aimed at camera, text, labels, floor, cast shadow or glow. Preserve actual transparent background, no baked checkerboard. Entire monster and feet inside the canvas with margins.

Precise local edit of ONLY THE MOUTH ORIENTATION in this image. Preserve the complete creature, rear abdomen, two clawed legs, exact pose, drawing style, color, framing and mouth position/overall height exactly. The camera is directly overhead. The current mouth is an almost flat ROUND DISK looking straight upward. Correct it into a SHORT ANATOMICAL HEAD inclined FORWARD TO THE LEFT. In the overhead view its circular opening MUST be foreshortened into a TALL OVAL, approximately 0.70-0.75 as wide horizontally as it is tall vertically. Do not leave a round circle. Its long ellipse axis is top-bottom on the canvas, not left-right. The near/front rim is on the LEFT, the far/back rim is on the RIGHT connected immediately into the body. Show a small difference in near/far lip thickness and a tiny exposed side wedge to make the forward lean obvious, but NO cylindrical neck, barrel, stacked flesh rings or long trumpet. Keep a COMPLETE UNBROKEN 360-degree ring of ivory triangular teeth around the entire OVAL perimeter, naturally compressed by foreshortening, including every side. Dark burgundy throat, simple broad shapes. Mouth remains compact and seated between the leg roots at the LEFT of the torso. Do not enlarge mouth or move it to right. Do not modify the right rear body at all. True transparent background, no floor, checkerboard, glow, labels, arrows or cast shadows. Do not rotate the body or camera.

Edit Image 1 into a more convincing finished CONCEPT of the SAME creature, following the owner's paintover notes in Image 2. Image 1 is the clean edit target, Image 2 is an instruction/placement guide ONLY: do not reproduce its arrows, text, white canvas or tiny diagram. Retain the exact overall creature footprint, two bent three-clawed running legs, left-facing front between those leg roots, right-facing tapered rear, subdued pale gray-pink flesh palette, clean dark contours and existing simple painted game style. The GAME CAMERA stays orthographic DIRECTLY OVERHEAD, 90 degrees down onto the BACK. Do NOT rotate the full body into a side/front/isometric view. Implement THREE SPECIFIC ART CORRECTIONS. (1) BACK: remove the current construction of overlapping petal-like muscle plates and disconnected modular chunks. Replace it with ONE coherent continuous stretched fleshy back/abdomen, low and compact, with a visible central spinal ridge and 5-6 pairs of CLEAR LARGE RIB ARCS sweeping out from that ridge beneath taut pale flesh. The ribs must be distinct elongated raised curved ridges, anatomically joined into one ribcage, NOT separate armor tiles, stacked meat slabs, circular sausage rings or a hard insect shell. Most surface areas remain simple and quiet. The rear narrows asymmetrically into the same compact blunt wedge, no rounded cap, forked fin or phallic tube. (2) HEAD ANGLE: the mouth-head must project FORWARD TO THE LEFT nearly horizontally along the ground, with only a modest upward pitch. It must not be a vertical round tooth-sticker pointing at the ceiling. Use a very short integrated head-root, a visible continuous TOP of the head behind the rim, and a naturally foreshortened oblique oval opening at the leading left edge, as seen by the overhead camera. The oval is tall top-bottom and narrow left-right due to its forward-facing angle; convincing near/far lip overlap communicates orientation. Do not create a long barrel, fleshy chimney, thick ring-stack collar or enormous trumpet. Keep the head compact, but its teeth very legible. (3) DENTITION: replace the uniform little single row with TWO TO THREE INTERLEAVED CIRCUMFERENTIAL ROWS of MUCH BIGGER irregular teeth. The tooth rings run all the way around the mouth, following its foreshortening. Use varied lengths and shapes: a few long hooked fangs, broader short triangular cutters, slightly crooked teeth; give 2-3 teeth a chipped tip or irregular worn edge. Off-white aged ivory with restrained warm roots, dark burgundy mouth interior. It must look like organic dangerous dentition, not perfectly spaced identical petals or a clean mechanical saw. Rows remain readable as separate depths; do not fill the throat with tiny white noise. Keep the intact dark throat visible. Tooth chips, not bloody wounds. No eyes, extra limbs, tongue, dripping blood, text, labels, arrows, shadows, floor or baked checkerboard. Preserve genuine alpha transparency and full creature framing with all claws included. This is one coherent overhead game monster, prioritizing silhouette, head orientation and ribs over fine texture.

Refine the SAME chosen Emergency Shift creature in Image 1. The owner says this version is CLOSE to their intended design: preserve its HEAD, forward-angled oval maw, layered irregular large teeth, mouth position at the LEFT front, continuous ribbed gray-pink back, compact right rear, overhead camera and overall identity. Make ONLY two focused improvements. CAMERA: strict orthographic CEILING VIEW, looking directly down at dorsal back and the tops of the two legs, feet lying on one horizontal floor plane. Do not show side-view legs or rotate the body. (1) REBUILD THE TWO LEGS WITH BELIEVABLE RUNNING ANATOMY. Current appendages look like odd splayed arms with huge hands. Keep exactly TWO clawed running legs rooted into a shared coherent muscular pelvis beside/just behind the mouth. Each must read as one connected chain: compact powerful proximal thigh, ONE clear knee, lean shank with visible broad tendon direction, compact ankle, then a SMALL ANIMAL FOOT with three forward-pointing clawed toes. No human palm, thumb, extra elbows, loose joints, sausage bead segments, disconnected toes or giant splayed hands. Toes and ivory claws point generally LEFT, the direction of travel, and bear weight on the same floor. Do not hide feet beneath the body. Show a natural asymmetric RUNNING CONTACT POSE: the upper leg reaches somewhat farther forward and is more open at the knee; the lower leg is more flexed and a little farther back in the stride. Their roots remain convincingly part of one pelvis, not independently stuck onto the head rim. Keep generous negative gaps around limbs and a lean fast silhouette, with claws proportionate rather than huge hooks. (2) MAKE THE RIBCAGE ORGANIC, NOT RULER-SYMMETRICAL. Retain the single continuous fleshy back and clear ribs. Give the central spinal ridge a slight natural shallow curve and a small offset from the exact geometric center as the pelvis twists with the running pose. The ribs on opposite sides must NOT be perfectly mirrored, evenly spaced, same-length repeated arcs. Vary length, spacing and curvature moderately; a few ribs are partly covered by a different thickness of muscle/taut skin, one side opens a little more than the other. Preserve credible skeletal organization rather than random crooked noise, injury or broken anatomy. The rear outline is gently uneven and tapered, not a phallic rounded cap and not a decorative fork. Broad legible forms, muted flesh, thin dark contour and restrained shading matching the input; no extra microtexture, gore, glow, floor, cast shadow, labels or text. Preserve genuine alpha transparency and all complete limbs within comfortable canvas margins.

Local refinement of ONLY THE BACK/RIBS in this creature. Preserve the head, exact tilted mouth and teeth, both newly shaped running legs and feet, their asymmetric stride, palette, framing and strict overhead camera. The back is still too neatly mirrored: the ribs are paired repeated teardrops along a straight divider. Make these SPECIFIC visible organic differences while retaining one believable ribcage: (A) give the central dorsal ridge a shallow but clearly perceptible S-curve, lower on the canvas near the shoulder and slightly higher toward the rear, instead of a ruler-straight center line; (B) on the UPPER side, the second and third rib arcs are shorter and partly concealed under one broad unbroken patch of taut skin, with a larger gap after them; the fourth upper arc is longer and swept backward; (C) on the LOWER side, keep two broad front rib arcs, then three more subtly outlined ribs with different spacing and thickness; these must not line up one-for-one with the upper arcs; (D) make one rear rib curve partly disappear beneath a small overlapping continuous MUSCLE FOLD, not an armor plate. Broad areas of smooth flesh between ribs are important so it is not a complete accordion or evenly quilted shell. The two outer sides differ slightly in fullness as the torso twists in a running pose, but the whole abdomen retains its compact tapered outline. Restraint: moderate asymmetry, coherent load-bearing anatomy, no random dents, wounds, broken bones, cysts, clutter or extra appendages. Do not use identical mirrored rib shapes or equal intervals. No hard exoskeleton, modular meat plates, rear rounded cap or forked tail. Keep the clean concept rendering, no extra microtexture, no floor, glow, cast shadows, text or labels, and true alpha transparency.

Substantially simplify and improve this SAME Emergency Shift creature concept for future articulated 2D animation. Preserve its identity: two clawed running limbs, large forward-tilted oval tooth-ring mouth at LEFT between the limb roots, pale gray-pink flesh, tapered compact rear to RIGHT, TRUE 90-DEGREE ORTHOGRAPHIC TOP VIEW of its back. This is a coherent movable living creature, NOT an anatomy chart, muscle kit, rigid decorative shell or production rig sheet. MOST IMPORTANT — ONE FLEXIBLE BODY: replace the carved separate muscles and petal/slab divisions with ONE UNBROKEN SOFT SKIN ENVELOPE. The back is a continuous pliable fleshy mass with a gently curved longitudinal midline and only 4-5 broad unequal rib hints under stretched skin. Some rib hints fade completely under soft flesh; the two sides differ modestly. No fully outlined individual muscle islands, no isolated balls, no identical ribs, no ruler symmetry, no hard armor, and no repeated circular body segments. Give the torso a mild natural lateral curve and smooth silhouette that could plausibly bend more or straighten during movement without plates breaking apart. Rear is a simple uneven tapered low wedge, not a phallic cylindrical cap or fork. ARTICULATED LIMBS: exactly TWO complete limbs with coherent attached roots, one clear proximal joint, knee-like bend and compact wrist/ankle-foot transition. Each limb has broad simple continuous muscle/tendon masses, NOT a stack of bulges or beads. Roots have soft skin overlap and clear clearance for rotation, no stiff flap bridging the limb to the side of the back. The two limbs occupy different phases of a fast running/crawling step: one reaches forward LEFT and bears weight; the other is bent and a bit farther back. Their three compact forward-pointing clawed toes touch the same floor plane. No human palm/thumb, extra joints, detached claws or red bracelet-like cuffs around every toe. Ivory claws grow from the toes with natural cuticle attachment. Retain complete visible joints and enough negative space for future leg motion. HEAD: keep the compact anatomical root and forward-leaning oval mouth, 2-3 interleaved circumferential rows of irregular large ivory teeth, a few chipped or worn edges, dark maroon throat. Do not return to a flat vertical tooth sticker, tubular barrel neck, symmetrical flower teeth or a new eye. BLOOD DIRT — CLEAR AND IRREGULAR: the creature has recently fed. Add conspicuous dark crimson and burgundy BLOOD SMEARS on the outer mouth/lower lip and roots of several teeth, a few scraped streaks across the nearby front skin, and uneven blood staining on one forefoot's claws/toes. Add one broader rubbed blood mark along one flank, with sparse smaller attached flecks on the opposite side. Mix darker dried areas with a small amount of fresh red, but no bright red coating everywhere and no glossy neon. Keep large clean pale skin areas so the body, ribs and joints remain legible. Blood follows contact/smear directions, not uniform procedural speckles over every surface; no detached splatters, blood puddle, new wounds or background props. DRAWING: same graphic game creature family, restrained dark contour, 2-3 broad matte tones per form, much less microtexture and fine anatomy rendering than input. Prioritize a clear simple silhouette, plausible connected joints and deformable back. One creature, no text, labels, arrows, inset diagrams, cast shadow, floor, checkerboard or glow. Actual transparent background with comfortable framing around all claws.

Create an ALTERNATE MOTION-CHECK POSE of this EXACT SAME creature, not a redesign or a sprite sheet. Preserve its identity, total count of TWO limbs with three claws each, all proportions, the continuous pale blood-smeared skin, exact blood stain landmarks, the same asymmetrically hinted rib structure, the left/front angled oval maw with the same tooth arrangement, and the tapered right rear. Strict 90-degree orthographic OVERHEAD camera, actual transparent background. Pose change: gently BEND THE CONTINUOUS BACK sideways by about 15-20 degrees so the rear body curves toward the TOP of the canvas while the front still aims LEFT. The midline and faint ribs follow the bend continuously; outer side stretches slightly, inner side compresses into only one or two broad skin folds. No disconnected muscle plates, broken backbone, extra body segments, detached parts or sharpened fins. Swap the running contact phase: the LOWER limb reaches a little farther forward LEFT and opens its knee, the UPPER limb draws back and flexes at its same knee and ankle. Feet remain plausible load-bearing three-clawed animal feet on one XY floor plane, not human hands. No new joints, toes or limbs. Keep clear gaps between limbs and the body to demonstrate range of movement. The head moves with the front of the torso; do not independently rotate the mouth toward camera or change it into a circle sticker. Preserve layered irregular teeth and mouth blood. Restrained broad shading, do not add detail. One complete creature centered with margins, no labels, arrows, technical rig marks, motion streaks, floor or cast shadow. This pose must visibly demonstrate a flexible back and independently movable articulated legs while remaining recognizably the same animal.
